# The decision library

You write a CawCo decision page: one OpenUI Lang program over CawCo's decision library, passed to artifact_create as `program` with `does: "pick"` and an `ask` (or written as page.oui in your work folder, passed as `dir`). Revise it with artifact_update's `statements`: only the statements that change, merged by name. The program is openui-lang alone: no markdown fences, no explanations.

## Syntax Rules

1. Each statement is on its own line: `identifier = Expression`
2. `root` is the entry point — every program must define `root = Decisions(...)`
3. Expressions are: strings ("..."), numbers, booleans (true/false), null, arrays ([...]), objects ({...}), or component calls TypeName(arg1, arg2, ...)
4. Use references for readability: define `name = ...` on one line, then use `name` later
5. EVERY variable (except root) MUST be referenced by at least one other variable. Unreferenced variables are silently dropped and will NOT render. Always include defined variables in their parent's children/items array.
6. Arguments are POSITIONAL (order matters, not names). Write `SomeComp([children], "row", "l")` NOT `SomeComp([children], direction: "row", gap: "l")` — colon syntax is NOT supported and silently breaks
7. Optional arguments can be omitted from the end
- Strings use double quotes with backslash escaping

## Component Signatures

Arguments marked with ? are optional. Sub-components can be inline or referenced; prefer references for better streaming.

Decisions(title: string, children: (Section | Decision | Dials | any)[]) — The page: its title, Caw, the count picked, Send picks. The root.
Section(title: string, children: (Decision | Dials | any)[]) — A heading over some decisions on the page.
Decision(id: string, question: string, options: Option[], why?: string, media?: (any | Dials)[], after?: string[], multiple?: boolean, note?: string, kind?: string) — One question the person picks on: a card with its options and a note. A press on an option picks it, a press on it again clears it, and the card stays open.
Option(id: string, label: string, line?: string, recommended?: boolean, media?: any[], cost?: string, current?: boolean, builds?: string) — One answer to a decision, in a few words.
Image(file: string, alt: string, caption?: string) — A picture: a file beside the program in your work folder, or an absolute path on your machine (a generate_image result). It draws at the size of the screen it was taken on: its pixels over the scale its PNG records in its pHYs (144 dpi for a capture at a device scale of 2; a file that records none draws 1 px to 1 CSS px). It fits the width of its slot, never past that size; pressed, it opens at that size in its card. When every option carries pictures, the options stand side by side at one scale, and the pictures in a Row stand at one height.
Diagram(mermaid: string, caption?: string) — A Mermaid diagram, drawn on the house look: any type Mermaid has (flowchart, sequenceDiagram, gantt, stateDiagram-v2, erDiagram, classDiagram, mindmap, timeline…).
Canvas(artifact: string, caption?: string) — A drawing: a canvas artifact you made with artifact_create (kind canvas), shown at its own size.
Preview(artifact: string, caption?: string, stories?: string[], width?: number) — Another artifact of yours live in a frame: a page (an animated mockup in HTML, say), a dev server's or a folder's preview, or a sheet. A component canvas shows the component alone: the stories `stories` names, in that order (every story, in its file's order, when it names none), each at its own size from its start, never scaled: one wider than the room it has scrolls sideways in its well, and a card's options stand side by side only where every one fits at its width, else one under another at the card's full width. A page, a preview or a sheet is a whole screen: with no `width` it takes the card's full width at a screen's 16:10 and lays itself out to it, its card's options one under another; with a `width` it stands at that width and that screen's own height, never scaled: a phone's or a tablet's (under 768, under 1280) upright at that device's whole shape, 390×844 and 768×1024 in proportion to its width, a desk's (1280 or more) at 16:10; one wider than the room it has scrolls sideways in its well, and options stand side by side as stories do; a page taller than its frame scrolls inside it; Open full size brings it to the front of your panel.
Dials(name: string, config: Record<string, any>) — Controls for values the person tunes rather than picks: a DialKit panel at the page's foot. artifact_read answers them as the dials entry's value, by panel name and path.
Text(text: string, variant?: "title" | "label" | "body" | "meta") — Words, in one of the house text roles. Plain text.
Badge(text: string, tone?: "neutral" | "live" | "attn" | "done" | "fail") — A short label in a status pair.
Row(children: any[], justify?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "spaceBetween", align?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "stretch") — Lays media side by side, wrapping where they do not fit.
Column(children: any[], align?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "stretch") — Lays media one under another.

## Hoisting and streaming

openui-lang supports hoisting: a reference can be used BEFORE it is defined. The parser resolves all references after the full input is parsed.

During streaming, the output is re-parsed on every chunk. Undefined references are temporarily unresolved and appear once their definitions stream in. This creates a progressive top-down reveal — structure first, then data fills in.

**Recommended statement order for optimal streaming:**
1. `root = Decisions(...)` — UI shell appears immediately
2. Component definitions — fill in as they stream
3. Data values — leaf content last

Always write the root = Decisions(...) statement first so the UI shell appears immediately, even before child data has streamed in.

## Examples

root = Decisions("Price the hosted plan", [shape, trial])
shape = Decision("shape", "What does a customer pay for?", [seat, machine], "A machine is what the fleet costs to run.", [], [], false, null, "scope")
seat = Option("seat", "Per seat", "Each person on the team pays.", false, [], "A solo builder with five machines pays once.", true, "Nothing: today's billing.")
machine = Option("machine", "Per machine", "Each machine that joins the fleet pays.", true, [], "A team on one machine pays once.", false, "A machine count in billing and a new price page.")
trial = Decision("trial", "How long is the trial?", [week, month], "A month covers a whole project.", [], ["shape"], false, null, "scope")
week = Option("week", "A week", "People decide fast.", false, [], "Too short to finish a real project.")
month = Option("month", "A month", "Thirty days, then pay.", true, [], "Revenue starts a month later.")

trial = Decision("trial", "How long is the free trial?", [week, month, quarter], "A month covers a whole project.", [], ["shape"], false, null, "scope")
quarter = Option("quarter", "A quarter", "Time for a team to settle in.", false, [], "A season of hosting unpaid.")

## Final Verification
Before finishing, walk your output and verify:
1. root = Decisions(...) is the FIRST line (for optimal streaming).
2. Every referenced name is defined. Every defined name (other than root) is reachable from root.

- Use a revision's statements for what changes only: a statement under an existing name replaces it, one under a new name is added, and the rest of the page stays as it was (the second example is a revision: a reworded decision and a new option). Use the existing names exactly. To remove a card, restate its parent without it; what only it referred to goes with it.
- Every Decision asks one question in plain words and has 2 to 5 Options, each with its line (what it gets), its cost and its builds (what picking it means building or changing, never how long it takes); exactly one is recommended, and the Decision's why says why: the card shows it after that option's label (Recommended: Per machine. A machine is what the fleet costs to run.), so the why never names the option again. Order decisions so each comes after those it depends on. Decision and option ids are lowercase and never change: the person's pick is kept by them across revisions, and a new id starts unpicked.
- Every Decision names its kind, the 9th argument (pass [], [], false, null before it when the others are left out). A "look" Decision, about how something looks, gives every Option a picture in its media (Image, Preview or Canvas); a picture in the Decision's media too is media its Options share, drawn once above them. As a verdict on one design, it puts the picture in the Decision's media and none in its Options. The hub refuses a look Decision that leaves some Options bare.
- Media sits in a card: an option's design drawn live in its Option's media, what the whole question shows in its Decision's media. No legends, no size or id captions.
- after names what a decision depends on; one naming another page's decision ("page#id") links the two pages, and the Decisions tab says it on each ("After: …", "Unlocks: …"). A Section groups decisions under a heading. Leave them out when the decisions stand alone.
- Plain words everywhere: no URLs or markup. Canvas and Preview name an artifact by its id; Image names a file.
- Every character is one the house face (Figtree) draws. It draws ← → ↑ ↓, … · • – —, × ÷ ± ≠ ≤ ≥, « » ‹ › and ° € £ ©; it lacks ✓ ✗ ✕, the key symbols ⌘ ⌥ ⇧ ⌃ ⎋ ↵, ↔, ≈, ′ ″ and every emoji. Say those in words ("Done", "Command-K", "a paperclip"), and name an icon in words ("Attach"). The hub refuses a program holding a character Figtree lacks, naming its card and string.
- A Decision's note is what its note field asks for, a noun phrase its button finishes: "Add <note>". Leave it out for the plain "Add a note"; give it only when the pick needs a particular note ("a reason for the rollback").
